correctness.rationale: The positive Legendre weights yield uniform convergence and a Schoenberg positive-semidefinite kernel; degree 4j+1 parity gives equatorial oddness. The uniform interior Darboux formula with controlled differentiated remainder reduces the series near the equator to a weighted sine sum plus O_alpha(|h|). Abelian Riemann sums give the fractional exponent/coefficient, integrating -log(2 sin(t/2)) gives the critical logarithm, and termwise derivative uniform convergence for alpha>3/2 gives the stated exact negative central slope. The analytic full-degree Legendre generating mixture is strictly positive definite without altering dominant singular terms. Independently checked fractional constants against the exact published Gamma forms (alpha=1.2,1.4), and the identity follows for all via Gamma reflection. Finite checker source was inspected, not treated as proof of series asymptotics.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Published fractional theorem covers *arbitrary* nonnegative tails with O(j^-s-delta) error, not only exact zeta-normalized powers; published critical theorem likewise permits perturbations and strict-positive-definite analytic additions. These are stronger than both singular regimes of the target.

originality.rationale: Two previously published SCOPE articles from 2026-11-16 are strictly more general at the only nontrivial cusp regimes: Sharp fractional equatorial cusps for subcritical positive-definite Legendre spectra covers all positive coefficient tails A(j+1)^-s+O(j^-s-delta) for 1<s<3/2, while A universal sharp logarithmic equatorial cusp for positive-definite Legendre series covers general critical s=3/2 coefficient tails and analytic SPD admixture. Setting A=1/zeta(alpha) gives exactly the submitted formulas. The remaining alpha>3/2 finite central slope follows routinely from summable differentiated Legendre expansion and is not a distinctive new result.
residual_risks: The two dominating published records share publication date 2026-11-16 with the assigned record, so no unverified precise time-of-day priority claim is made. Scientific claim implication/coverage is nonetheless decisive.
A useful exposition can combine regimes, but mere aggregation of already-proved sharp cases plus routine smooth case does not create an independently new valuable theorem.

final_claim: For alpha>1, normalized nonnegative Legendre weights (j+1)^-alpha on degrees 4j+1 have an equatorial signed |h|^(alpha-1/2) cusp for 1<alpha<3/2, a sharp h log(1/|h|) cusp at alpha=3/2, and a finite negative derivative for alpha>3/2, preserved at the singular orders after analytic strictly positive-definite mixing.
